]

This invocation produces exactly ONE independent R7-D1-M1 poster, assigned portrait width:height 2:3.
COMMON COORDINATOR CONSTRAINTS:
[
  "Print the supplied title exactly once, with intact readable Hangul and the original word spacing. Line breaks may occur between whole words. The directions are internal guidance and must not be printed.",
  "No other copy, supporting text, labels, numbers, logos, series identifiers, style names or watermarks. Depicted clothing, objects and surfaces must be unbranded and free of incidental text.",
  "Each assigned maker produces only its own independent, single flat opaque poster, portrait 2:3. No panels, contact sheets, poster mockups or borrowing another maker's generated image as a reference.",
  "The substantial non-glyph relation must remain recognizable with the title hidden and at reduced viewing size. Tiny ornament, wallpaper, background texture, gradients and 3D lettering alone do not satisfy it.",
  "Preserve the assigned relation and distinction while solving practical crop, proportion, palette, alignment and title placement independently. There is no shared title-object-footer layout or common allocation of image and copy area.",
  "Downstream native-tool production must request the maximum resolution supported by the current tool and model while preserving 2:3; verify the actual returned dimensions and readable copy after generation."
]

DESIGN SPEC — use case photorealistic-natural; single finished flat opaque poster, edge-to-edge observational location photography.
요청한 화면 비율을 유지하면서 현재 도구와 모델이 지원하는 가능한 최대 해상도로 출력

Make different human paces coexist in one continuous inhabited pedestrian place, at one captured moment. A fixed, modestly elevated camera looks across a broad light-grey concrete pedestrian concourse, with understated real paving joints and a plain low wall at the far upper edge. No signs or incidental writing. Natural daylight from upper left, consistent perspective and light, dry matte pavement, credible foot contact and restrained actual surface detail. No studio stage, montage, collage, frame or mockup.

Two substantial full-body adults dominate the middle of the scene. Left of center, one adult in a plain dark navy overshirt and dark trousers has genuinely paused: face and body sharp, weight visibly settled through one planted leg and sole, other leg relaxed, hands naturally at sides. The pose must read as stationary even at small scale. To the right, another adult in a plain warm rust jacket and dark trousers passes laterally from left to right in a purposeful stride, photographed during a single sustained exposure. Their body is clearly recognizable as a moving person with coherent limbs and stride, but shows selective directional motion blur and a horizontal trailing smear. Keep the planted shoe contact and real moving bodily mass legible. Do not reduce the moving figure to decorative ribbons, disembodied streaks or a row of separate cloned figures. The still person, still ground and sharp title remain sharp; only the passer has motion blur. Both people have large enough silhouette mass to remain immediately distinct at thumbnail scale, and neither person's feet are cropped away.

Arrange the scene around the foot-level shared ground, not an image plus header/footer. The paused figure sits slightly farther back to the left; the passer moves across the closer right-hand part of that SAME plane. The title is the stationary point between the settled foot and the passing trajectory: place it on the open pavement in the lower middle of the inhabited scene, close to the paused person's planted foot and beside the path of the passer. Retain clear physical separation from shoes and blur. Let the concourse continue below it so it feels within the scene, never a bottom caption or remote top header. No artificial text box or empty graphic band.

Render the sole title exactly once: “서로 다른 속도”. Do not print quotation marks. One steady horizontal baseline; medium-weight, clear contemporary sans-serif Hangul, normal square syllable proportions, intact counters and strokes, conventional letter spacing and the exact two word spaces. Calm dark-charcoal type against sufficiently light pavement, fully sharp, substantial enough to read at reduced size but quieter than the human relation. Text is graphic poster typography aligned to the viewing plane, not distorted perspective paint on the floor. Do not stretch, warp, inflate or break syllables. No additional copy, labels, numbers, marks, logos, watermark, border or series identifier.

The first recognition is one person paused while another moves past; the title binds this bodily contrast. Quiet observational mood from posture, space and duration. Maintain real photographic material differences between clothing, skin, shoes and concrete. Avoid glamour lighting, generic cinematic glow, global motion blur, faux film borders, over-grained texture and decorative effects. Output only the single completed portrait 2:3 opaque poster.
